lesson.title: Every post leaves a trace
lesson.subtitle: What your digital footprint says about you

video.title: Every post leaves a trace
video.format_note: Animated explainer for students aged 12–16, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, the student's teacher (main character)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talking to the student)

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor in a science lab holds up a phone showing a stranger's public profile: a school badge, a cake, a bus stop, a cat.
scenes.animation: Profile tiles pop in one by one around the phone.
scenes.narration: In five minutes, I found a stranger's school, her birthday and the street she walks home on. I never met her. I only read her public posts.

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the cyber track chip.
scenes.narration: Today: your digital footprint, and how to make it say what you want.

scenes.visual: Two columns of footprints across a phone screen: bold ones (posts, photos) and faint ones (location, searches).
scenes.animation: Bold prints stamp in first, then faint ones fade in.
scenes.narration: Everything you do online leaves a trace, and together those traces are your digital footprint. Some you leave on purpose: posts, comments, photos and voice notes. That's your active footprint. Others you leave without noticing: where your phone goes, what you search for, what you like and watch. That's your passive footprint.

scenes.visual: A post on a phone; a camera flash shows a screenshot; copies fly into many chat bubbles; a delete button removes only the first copy.
scenes.narration: A footprint in sand washes away, but an online one usually stays. A friend can screenshot your post in one second. By evening, a group chat can forward it to hundreds of people. Deleting your copy doesn't delete theirs.

scenes.visual: Three separate photos: a uniform badge, a birthday cake, a bus stop sign. They slide together into one profile card.
scenes.narration: Here's what most people miss. One detail on its own looks harmless: your school uniform in one photo, your birthday in another, your bus stop in a third. Put together, they tell a stranger who you are, where to find you, and when.

scenes.visual: Jigsaw pieces with the same small pictures drop onto a table and join into a picture of a girl at a bus stop.
scenes.animation: Pieces click together one by one.
scenes.narration: It's like a jigsaw puzzle. One piece shows nothing, but every post adds a piece, and a patient stranger can finish the picture. Even your pet's name is a piece, because it's a common answer to the security questions that reset passwords.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor holds up three cards: a book, a school with a street sign, a house with a clock.
scenes.animation: Cards drop in with a small bounce.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Which of these is safest to put on a public profile?

scenes.visual: The book card gets the check badge; the other two fade.
scenes.narration: Your favourite book. It says what you like, not where you are or when you're alone.

scenes.visual: Three faces appear one by one beside a post: a grandmother, a head teacher, a shadowy stranger.
scenes.animation: Faces pop in as they are named.
scenes.narration: Before you post, try the three-people test. Would you be happy if your grandmother saw it? Your head teacher? A stranger who wants to find you? If any answer is no, change it, or keep it for close friends.

scenes.visual: A search result for a student's name shows a science project, a poem and a football award.
scenes.animation: Good results slide in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your footprint can work for you, too. Think of a science project you're proud of, a kind comment, or a skill you're learning. One day a school or an employer may search your name, so give them something good to find.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor points at a post with a delete button and a clock showing one hour.
scenes.narration: Your turn. You delete an embarrassing post after one hour. Is it gone for good?

scenes.visual: The 'not for sure' card gets the check badge, then four summary cards line up.
scenes.animation: Cards line up left to right.
scenes.on_screen_text: Trace · Add up · Test · Work for you
scenes.narration: Not for sure, because in one hour someone may have saved or shared it. Remember: everything leaves a trace, small details add up, test before you post, and make your footprint work for you.

scenes.visual: A student looks at her own profile on a phone, as if through a stranger's eyes, and taps 'hide' on one post.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: look at your profile the way a stranger would. Count the posts that show your school, your street or your routine, and hide or delete one of them.

checkpoints.prompt: Which of these is safest to put on a public profile?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — it says what you like, not where to find you or when you're alone.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — places and times tell a stranger where and when to find you. Your favourite book is the safe one.
